objective: Qualify one Community RTX 4090 host for all remaining validation-only two-stage GPU work after the RTX 3090 batch-extension thermal stop.

target_hardware.reason_for_cap: The RTX 3090 measured batch optimum was 8; batches 12/16/24 produced no throughput gain and triggered three software thermal-slowdown samples.

gate_sequence: verify the new GPU identity, CUDA tensor execution, package versions, uploaded file whitelist and exact data hashes
run the original Frozen-Qwen few-shot, separate-head DistilBERT and shared-adapter QLoRA execution/memory smokes on l2-a01
run the representative formal-length throughput benchmark at batches 2, 4, 6 and 8
run a sustained batch-8 Frozen-Qwen few-shot scoring soak and one complete 4,096-example formal-length QLoRA training soak without retaining a scientific checkpoint
audit logs, finite values, prediction variation, memory, temperature, power and every named NVIDIA slowdown reason
freeze the 4090 batch sizes and update the wall-time/cost plan only after every gate passes
admission_criteria: all processes and artifacts pass with failure_count zero
test_contract_count is zero and only train/validation are opened
all losses and scores are finite and scored probabilities are non-constant
no CUDA OOM, CUDA error or incompatible resume state
zero software-thermal, hardware-thermal, hardware-slowdown or power-brake samples in both the representative benchmark and sustained soak
batch 8 remains inside the memory boundary and does not reduce throughput relative to smaller registered batches
the complete 4,096-example QLoRA soak completes with finite loss and the exact registered max length, batch, accumulation and adapter recipe
stop_conditions: any official-test reference or uploaded test file
any failure, OOM, CUDA error or non-finite value
any incompatible resume or artifact hash
two or more active software-thermal samples, or any hardware-thermal, hardware-slowdown or power-brake sample
unexpected GPU identity, VRAM capacity or package/model revision
